q-67498.name: Question 1
q-67498.problem:
What is the $5$th term of the geometric sequence given below?

$$
f(n+1)=-\frac{1}{2}f(n),\,f(1)=80,\,n\ge 1
$$
q-67498.worked_solution:
We use the recursive formula to compute the terms of the sequence up to the $5$th term:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) & =80 \\ f(2) & =-\frac{1}{2}f(1)=-\frac{1}{2}(80)=-40 \\ f(3) & =-\frac{1}{2}f(2)=-\frac{1}{2}(-40)=20 \\ f(4) & =-\frac{1}{2}f(3)=-\frac{1}{2}(20)=-10 \\ f(5) & =-\frac{1}{2}f(4)=-\frac{1}{2}(-10)=5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(5)=5.$

EXPLANATION

We use the recursive formula to compute the terms of the sequence up to the 5th term:

f(1)=80f(2)=−12f(1)=−12(80)=−40f(3)=−12f(2)=−12(−40)=20f(4)=−12f(3)=−12(20)=−10f(5)=−12f(4)=−12(−10)=5

q-67501.name: Question 2
q-67501.problem:
Which of the three sequences below are geometric sequences?

I. $\frac{1}{4},\,\frac{1}{2},\,2,\,…$

II. ${a}_{n+1}=\frac{3}{2}{a}_{n},\,{a}_{1}=-1,\,n\ge 1$

III. $1,\,0.2,\,0.03,\,…$
q-67501.worked_solution:
A sequence is geometric if there is a common ratio between its terms. Let's check each sequence in turn.

- Sequence I is not a geometric sequence because not every pair of consecutive terms has the same ratio. To see this, we only need to go up to the third term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{(\frac{1}{4})} & =2 \\ \frac{{a}_{3}}{{a}_{2}}=\frac{2}{(\frac{1}{2})} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

- Sequence II is a geometric sequence. The recursive rule ${a}_{n+1}=\frac{3}{2}{a}_{n}$ tells us that each term is $\frac{3}{2}$ times the previous term, so the common ratio is $r=\frac{3}{2}.$

- Sequence III is not a geometric sequence because not every pair of consecutive terms has the same ratio. To see this, we only need to go up to the third term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{0.2}{1} & =0.2 \\ \frac{{a}_{3}}{{a}_{2}}=\frac{0.03}{0.2} & =0.15\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, only sequence II is a geometric sequence.

  • Sequence I is not a geometric sequence because not every pair of consecutive terms has the same ratio. To see this, we only need to go up to the third term: a2a1=(12)(14)=2a3a2=2(12)=4

  • Sequence II is a geometric sequence. The recursive rule an+1=32an tells us that each term is 32 times the previous term, so the common ratio is r=32.

q-79511.name: Question 3
q-79511.problem:
What is the $4$th term of the geometric sequence given below?

$$
{a}_{n+1}=-6{a}_{n},\,{a}_{1}=\frac{1}{36},\,n\ge 1
$$
q-79511.worked_solution:
We use the recursive formula to compute the terms of the sequence up to the $4$th term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =\frac{1}{36} \\ {a}_{2} & =-6{a}_{1}=-6(\frac{1}{36})=-\frac{1}{6} \\ {a}_{3} & =-6{a}_{2}=-6(-\frac{1}{6})=1 \\ {a}_{4} & =-6{a}_{3}=-6(1)=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${a}_{4}=-6.$
